prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (RDC; call sign Juniper) provides 24/7 EMS call intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, regional coordination/shared operational picture under approved clinical/jurisdictional protocols; jurisdictions retain resources/local policy. RDC records original caller report/clarifications, authorization time, and reason for assigned-unit selection; maintains regional coverage picture from unit locations/status, crew reports, readiness. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) validates location before medical details; captures symptoms, hazards, age, consciousness/breathing, chief reason/onset, observed vs hearsay, access barriers, callback; stays engaged; produces Caller Location Correction Slip. Computer Aided Dispatch Console (CAD Console) checks address/map data; shows current incident/priority, travel times, unit availability, constraints; presents staging options by demand/travel time/access. Staff verify currency. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) assigns/confirms priority, reviews uncertainty/conflict/deterioration/urgency disputes, records basis, confirms response, directs clarification, escalates severe ambiguity to Regional Medical Director; sends Pediatric Acuity Note. Regional Medical Director gives clinical policy/resource advice only. Shift Commander (Sundial) has operational authority; approves overcapacity/exceptions/nonstandard response/reduced coverage and reviews coverage picture before staging moves. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates unit position/status and recommends units by priority, capability, travel, crew readiness, coverage. Dispatcher authorizes per rules. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network, backups/checks; selects available talkgroup; verifies reachability; sends dispatch/priority/route changes; retransmits unclear discrepancies; if no prompt acknowledgment retries and alerts dispatch supervisor; confirms approved route changes before diversion; sends Coverage Gap Bulletin when ambulance coverage is below threshold. Dispatch transmission includes incident identifier, location, priority, assignment, immediate hazards; controlled handoff requires crew acknowledgment and dispatch confirmation of essentials. Paramedic Crew repeats location/priority, reports conflicts, material changes/status (available/responding/on scene/transporting/unavailable), and staging entry/exit position/status. Ambulance Unit 417 follows instructions; remains at staging until new location/direct assignment. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) reports restrictions/defects, produces Battery Swap, verifies maintenance clearance. North Gate Status Board/South Gate Status Board display access; dispatch states confirmed/uncertain gate or approach constraints. Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination information with receiving Emergency Department when required.

New part:
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
S138: Regional Dispatch Center uses the swap voucher to confirm that a unit's battery readiness is current before it is placed in service.
S139: Regional Dispatch Center uses the queue snapshot to account for congestion approaching the northern entry before assigning a route.
S140: North Gate Status Board displays the latest queue condition and access restriction for units approaching the northern entry.
S141: Triage Supervisor advises dispatch when changes in clinical demand may require repositioning available units.
S142: Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities that dispatch applies when assigning units during elevated demand.
S143: Hospital Liaison Desk provides receiving-facility capacity information for consideration during transport planning.
S144: Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving a unit away from its current area.
S145: Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location or status reports and routes corrections through the established operational process.
S146: Ambulance Coordination Platform retains time-stamped status changes so supervisors can review the sequence of unit movement.
S147: A crew advises dispatch when a road closure, unsafe condition, or unexpected delay makes the assigned route unsuitable.
S148: Regional Dispatch Center records the approved alternative route and checks that the change does not leave a critical area without reasonable coverage.
S149: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
S150: The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S151: The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
S152: The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
S153: The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
S154: Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
S155: The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
S156: The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S157: The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
S158: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
